signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + BoJ Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 160.01, testing the psychologically significant 160.00 handle as Middle East tensions escalate following reports of IRGC forces readying sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The pair remains supported by a 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential, yet the current spot level of 160.01 is the historically sensitive threshold that previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention. Options markets are aggressively pricing downside protection, with 25d Risk Reversals at -1.74 showing a strong put skew that contradicts the bid in spot. COT data shows JPY net short at -81,619 (pctl 9), confirming that the carry trade remains crowded and vulnerable to a disorderly unwind if geopolitical risk forces a VIX spike above 25. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage persists but intervention risk at 160.00 caps the immediate upside. Catalyst: China official PMIs on 31 August. Risk: Direct BoJ/MoF intervention or a VIX spike above 25 triggers a carry unwind toward SMA20 at 158.87.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/CHF is the primary G10 bilateral theme this week as the Australian Dollar outperforms G10 peers by an average of +1.181% while the Swiss Franc lags the complex at -0.658%. The leader-to-laggard spread has reached a critical 1.839% across available pairs, driven by a massive +435bp carry advantage in favor of AUD (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%). While retail sentiment is extremely short AUD/CHF at 95%, COT data shows AUD leveraged funds are net long +53,578 with a pctl(52w) of 95, indicating a crowded institutional long. The divergence between retail fading the move and institutions chasing the carry suggests trend continuation unless risk-off sentiment intensifies. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry-driven outperformance dominates while VIX remains at 14.4. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting on 2 September for broader Oceania sentiment. Risk: Sharp risk-off shift (VIX > 25) triggers a flight to CHF, rapidly compressing the carry spread.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Extreme + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD is trading at 1.1586, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1593) following hawkish Jackson Hole commentary from Fed Chair Warsh. COT positioning for EUR has collapsed to a net short of -55,311, representing a 3rd percentile extreme (z-score -2.28) within its 52-week range. Options markets are pricing a 2.4-point Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.7%), signaling elevated demand for protection despite the spot decline. Fed holds at 3.75%. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; extreme spec shorts and carry disadvantage favor a test of the SMA50 at 1.149. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 September. Risk: A soft US jobs print on Friday leads to a repricing of Fed hike odds, triggering a short squeeze in the crowded EUR short.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + ESI Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3534, holding just below the SMA20 at 1.3540 as technical momentum stalls. Speculative positioning is currently at a 96th percentile extreme (lev_net +56,839), suggesting the bullish Cable trend is reaching a point of exhaustion. This crowded long is increasingly at odds with the Economic Surprise Index (ESI) for GBP, which has fallen to -8.8 as UK data begins to underperform expectations. While the 10Y UK-US yield spread of +43bp provides a nominal buffer, the GBP real policy rate of +0.35% is significantly lower than the USD real rate of +1.45%. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish GBP/USD; crowded positioning and negative ESI signal risk of a long-unwind. Catalyst: US August jobs data on 4 September. Risk: US data misses, weakening the USD and allowing the GBP long to extend toward 1.3600.
